title: Retry Budget
statement: Implement `solve(outcomes, budget)`. `outcomes` is a list of `ok` or `fail` in the order attempts would happen. You may consume at most `budget` outcomes. Stop at the first `ok` and return `{"attempts": used, "result": "ok"}`. If the budget runs out or the list runs out on failures, return `{"attempts": used, "result": "fail"}`. Do not read past the budget.
constraints: attempts counts outcomes you actually consumed
hints: Increment used before you look at the outcome, and stop when used would exceed budget.
If you never see ok, the result is fail and attempts is how many you consumed.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A retry loop has two exits: success, and the budget.

editorial: A retry loop has two exits: success, and the budget. Consuming an outcome past the budget is the bug, even if a later ok exists. The attempts field is the number of outcomes read, which is what a metric would increment.
